RuleName: DB2 FK header query uses CONSTNAME instead of REFKEYNAME
RootCause: catalog_fk_query selected RTRIM(REFKEYNAME) AS fk_name from SYSCAT.REFERENCES. REFKEYNAME is the referenced parent constraint name not the FK own name. This caused FK names in the header to be the PK name instead of the FK constraint name leading to pairing failures and many false SOURCE_ONLY/TARGET_ONLY errors.
Fix: Changed SELECT to use RTRIM(CONSTNAME) AS fk_name. CONSTNAME is the actual foreign key constraint name in SYSCAT.REFERENCES.
MigrationContext: DB2 to Azure SQL MI migration. SYSCAT.REFERENCES stores both CONSTNAME (FK name) and REFKEYNAME (referenced PK/unique constraint name). The schema converter preserves CONSTNAME as the FK identity.
AdditionalInfo: Previously caused ~19 extra false FK_MISMATCH errors per database. All FK names were wrong causing downstream column pair lookup failures and signature mismatch.

RuleName: DB2 FK columns query replaced non-existent SYSCAT.REFKEYCOLUSE with proper KEYCOLUSE join
RootCause: catalog_fk_columns_query queried SYSCAT.REFKEYCOLUSE which does not exist as a DB2 catalog view. The query silently returned empty results causing all source_column_pairs to be empty in the report.
Fix: Replaced with a three-table JOIN: SYSCAT.REFERENCES joined to SYSCAT.KEYCOLUSE (for FK child columns via CONSTNAME) and LEFT JOIN SYSCAT.KEYCOLUSE again (for referenced PK columns via REFKEYNAME and COLSEQ).
MigrationContext: DB2 catalog has SYSCAT.KEYCOLUSE for all key columns (PK FK unique). To get fk_column->pk_column pairs you must join KEYCOLUSE twice: once for the FK side and once for the PK side using REFKEYNAME.
AdditionalInfo: This was the root cause of empty source_column_pairs in DetailsJson. The query now correctly returns fk_column and pk_column for every FK column position.

RuleName: DB2 RESTRICT (R) normalized to NO_ACTION for migration comparison
RootCause: DB2 update_action code R (RESTRICT) was mapped to RESTRICT but Azure SQL has no RESTRICT keyword. Migration tools convert RESTRICT to NO_ACTION. Comparing RESTRICT vs NO_ACTION produced 13 false FK_MISMATCH errors with description Referenced table mismatch.
Fix: Changed _db2_fk_delete_update mapping: R now maps to NO_ACTION instead of RESTRICT. Both RESTRICT and NO_ACTION prevent parent deletion when child rows exist.
MigrationContext: DB2 RESTRICT = immediate check prevents parent delete/update. Azure SQL NO_ACTION = deferred check at statement end same effect. Azure SQL does not support RESTRICT keyword so migration always converts to NO_ACTION.
AdditionalInfo: Eliminated all 13 remaining FK errors. DB2 action codes: A=NO_ACTION C=CASCADE R=NO_ACTION(was RESTRICT) N=NO_ACTION L=SET_NULL D=SET_DEFAULT.

RuleName: Cross-schema ref_schema comparison for USERID to dbo mapping
RootCause: FK ref_schema from DB2 (e.g. USERID) differs from Azure (e.g. dbo) by design. Naive string comparison of ref_schema would flag every FK as Referenced table mismatch even when ref_table names are identical.
Fix: _fk_ref_tables_match function checks if source ref_schema matches the declared source_schema (or resolved_source_schema) AND target ref_schema matches the declared target_schema. If both sides reference their own schema the FK is considered matching.
MigrationContext: In DB2-to-Azure migration the schema qualifier changes (USERID->dbo) but the table and column structure is preserved. The function accepts resolved_source_schema as fallback when the DB2 username differs from the logical schema name.
AdditionalInfo: Handles cases where resolved schema differs from logical schema e.g. actual DB2 user INFOQFIT vs logical USERID.

RuleName: Relaxed FK column row lookup when table_name in column metadata differs from header
RootCause: DB2 SYSCAT catalog can return different table names in FK header (TABNAME from SYSCAT.REFERENCES) vs FK column detail (FKTABNAME from column query). E.g. header says ADVISE_INDEX but column rows say ALT_CHILD_TAB for the same FK.
Fix: _fk_col_rows_for_fk first tries strict match on (table_name + fk_name). If no match it falls back to matching by fk_name only. If all such rows belong to a single table_name they are returned.
MigrationContext: With R002 fix (using KEYCOLUSE join) the table_name now comes from ref.TABNAME consistently. This fallback remains as safety net for edge cases.
AdditionalInfo: Previously caused FKs like SQL150521162547730 on ADVISE_INDEX to have empty column pairs because the strict table_name match failed.

RuleName: Greedy orphan FK pairing for unequal signature bucket sizes
RootCause: When the number of source FKs and target FKs in a logical signature bucket differs a simple zip would leave FKs unpaired producing false SOURCE_ONLY or TARGET_ONLY. E.g. 2 DB2 FKs vs 1 Azure FK on the same child table and ref table.
Fix: _fk_greedy_orphan_pairs scores all (source target) FK combinations by: exact name match (highest priority) then ref/column/action agreement then common constraint name prefix. Greedy matching picks best pairs first.
MigrationContext: During migration FK names may be regenerated (e.g. SQL150521162547730 vs SQL150521162547750). Greedy pairing ensures the best available match is used before declaring orphans.
AdditionalInfo: Uses _fk_orphan_pair_sort_key with scoring: 8*refs_ok + 4*pairs_match + 2*actions_match plus common prefix length as tiebreaker.

RuleName: Signature-based FK pairing uses FK-column-only key for loose matching
RootCause: DB2 and Azure often return different PK column names in catalog for the same FK. Matching on full fk->pk pair strings produced false orphans.
Fix: _fk_signature function creates (child_table ref_table ordered_fk_columns) key ignoring pk_column names. _fk_loose_bucket_key uses frozenset of FK column names for even looser grouping.
MigrationContext: The loose bucket groups FKs that reference the same parent table with the same set of child FK columns regardless of PK column naming or column order.
AdditionalInfo: Three-pass pairing: 1) exact (table_name fk_name) 2) signature (child_table ref_table ordered_fk_cols) 3) loose bucket (child_table ref_table fk_col_set).

RuleName: Column count lookup fallback for CREATOR vs TABSCHEMA mismatch
RootCause: Index high column count note showed source_columns=0 because src_col_counts was keyed by (TABSCHEMA table_name) from SYSCAT.COLUMNS but pairs used (CREATOR table_name) from SYSIBM.SYSTABLES. When CREATOR != TABSCHEMA the lookup returned 0.
Fix: _col_count_lookup first tries exact (schema table) match. If not found falls back to matching by table name only across all entries.
MigrationContext: DB2 has two table metadata systems: SYSIBM.SYSTABLES (uses CREATOR) and SYSCAT.TABLES (uses TABSCHEMA). They should be equal but can differ in some DB2 configurations.
AdditionalInfo: Example: SNAPDB table had 148 destination columns but source showed 0 due to schema key mismatch.

RuleName: Fallback column count query using SYSIBM.SYSCOLUMNS (TBCREATOR)
RootCause: Primary column count query uses SYSCAT.COLUMNS filtered by TABSCHEMA. When TABSCHEMA filter returns no rows (because tables are registered under CREATOR only) all column counts are zero.
Fix: Added catalog_columns_query_by_creator method using SYSIBM.SYSCOLUMNS with TBCREATOR filter. validate_indexes tries primary query first; if empty retries with TBCREATOR fallback.
MigrationContext: SYSIBM.SYSCOLUMNS is the legacy DB2 column catalog using TBCREATOR/TBNAME. SYSCAT.COLUMNS is the newer view using TABSCHEMA/TABNAME. Both should contain the same data but the filter column differs.
AdditionalInfo: Ensures source column counts are populated even when SYSCAT.COLUMNS TABSCHEMA does not match the schema used for SYSIBM.SYSTABLES CREATOR.

RuleName: Legacy CSV populates both source and destination columns for table-scoped objects
RootCause: For SOURCE_ONLY or TARGET_ONLY FK/index/check_constraint rows the legacy CSV left SourceObjectName or DestinationObjectName empty. This was misleading because these objects are scoped to a table that exists on both sides.
Fix: _legacy_both_sides_table_context fills both SourceObjectName/SourceSchemaName and DestinationObjectName/DestinationSchemaName with the child table context for foreign_keys indexes and check_constraints validation types.
MigrationContext: Table-scoped objects (FKs indexes constraints) differ from table_presence rows. A missing FK still belongs to a table that exists on both sides so both columns should show the table name for readability.
AdditionalInfo: Does NOT apply to table_presence rows where one side truly does not exist.

RuleName: Azure SQL FK action code normalization from integers and strings
RootCause: Azure SQL sys.foreign_keys returns delete_referential_action and update_referential_action as integers (0=NO_ACTION 1=CASCADE 2=SET_NULL 3=SET_DEFAULT) but JDBC/ODBC drivers may also return string names.
Fix: _azure_fk_delete_update tries int conversion first mapping 0-3 to standard names. Falls through to string uppercase normalization for string values. Defaults to NO_ACTION.
MigrationContext: Handles both pyodbc (returns integers) and JDBC (may return strings) driver behavior transparently.
AdditionalInfo: Maps: 0=NO_ACTION 1=CASCADE 2=SET_NULL 3=SET_DEFAULT. String fallback handles CASCADE NO_ACTION etc.

RuleName: DB2 FK action code normalization from single-letter codes
RootCause: DB2 SYSCAT.REFERENCES stores DELETERULE and UPDATERULE as single-letter codes. Without normalization comparison against Azure full-word values always fails.
Fix: _db2_fk_delete_update maps: A=NO_ACTION C=CASCADE R=NO_ACTION N=NO_ACTION L=SET_NULL D=SET_DEFAULT. Uses mp.get with fallback to raw code.
MigrationContext: R was originally mapped to RESTRICT (updated to NO_ACTION in R003). A and N both map to NO_ACTION per DB2 documentation.
AdditionalInfo: Updated 2026-05-13: R changed from RESTRICT to NO_ACTION per R003.

RuleName: FK mismatch description priority: ref_table > columns > actions
RootCause: Need clear categorization of FK differences for the report. Multiple things can differ (ref table columns actions) and the error description should reflect the most significant one.
Fix: _fk_mismatch_description returns: Referenced table mismatch (if ref_table or ref_schema differs) > Foreign key column mapping mismatch (if column pairs differ) > Foreign key delete/update rule mismatch (if only actions differ).
MigrationContext: Signature-paired FKs that only differ in Referenced table (schema difference) are downgraded to WARNING status since schema renaming is expected in migration.
AdditionalInfo: Priority order ensures the most critical difference is surfaced first in the report.

RuleName: High column count threshold raised from 120 to 250
RootCause: Original threshold of 120 columns was too low producing noisy INFO rows for tables like SNAPDB (148 columns) that are normal for the workload. These info rows cluttered the report without adding value.
Fix: Changed default in _many_col_threshold from 120 to 250. Still configurable via DV_MANY_COLUMNS_THRESHOLD env var.
MigrationContext: Large DB2 tables commonly have 120-200 columns. A threshold of 250 filters out normal wide tables and only flags truly exceptional ones. Override with DV_MANY_COLUMNS_THRESHOLD env var if needed.
AdditionalInfo: Previous threshold flagged SNAPDB (148 cols) and similar tables. New threshold eliminates these false info rows.

RuleName: Column count query retry with source_schema fallback when resolved_src returns empty
RootCause: _build_col_counts used resolved_src for the column query. If resolved_src differs from source_schema and neither SYSCAT.COLUMNS (TABSCHEMA) nor SYSIBM.SYSCOLUMNS (TBCREATOR) matched resolved_src the column counts were all zero.
Fix: Added fallback: if src_cc is empty after resolved_src queries retry _build_col_counts with original source_schema. Also wrapped both column queries in try/except to prevent crashes from catalog permission issues.
MigrationContext: resolved_src may be the actual DB2 username (e.g. INFOQFIT) while source_schema is the logical name (e.g. USERID). Column catalog may be keyed under either one. The retry ensures both are attempted.
AdditionalInfo: Covers the edge case where SYSCAT.COLUMNS has TABSCHEMA=USERID but resolved_src=INFOQFIT and vice versa. try/except prevents catalog query failures from blocking the entire index validation.

RuleName: Smart identity sequence filtering: exclude only when parent table exists on target
RootCause: DB2 identity sequences (SEQTYPE=I) migrate to Azure IDENTITY columns not sys.sequences. Simply excluding all identity sequences hid genuinely missing ones (e.g. ADDRESS table missing → its identity sequence is also truly missing). Need conditional logic: exclude identity sequences only when their parent table exists on Azure.
Fix: DB2 query now returns SEQTYPE and parent_table (via LEFT JOIN COLIDENTATTRIBUTES). Python layer in validate_table_presence builds tgt_table_names set and filters: identity sequences whose parent table EXISTS on target are removed (migrated as IDENTITY); identity sequences whose parent table is MISSING are kept (genuinely missing).
MigrationContext: DB2 SYSCAT.SEQUENCES.SEQTYPE: S=Standalone I=Identity A=Alias. COLIDENTATTRIBUTES links identity sequences to their parent table via SEQID. Azure sys.sequences only has standalone sequences; identity cols are in sys.identity_columns.
AdditionalInfo: Example: ADDRESS table missing in Azure → identity sequence SQL170429192751140 reported as PRESENCE_MISSING_IN_TARGET. RECORD_ERROR_MESSAGE table exists in Azure → its identity sequence SQL150528150217890 is excluded (migrated as IDENTITY).

RuleName: ObjectType for views shown as VIEW instead of TABLE across all validators
RootCause: All data validators (row_counts column_nulls distinct_keys checksum referential_integrity constraint_integrity) and behavior validators hardcoded object_type as TABLE in detail dicts. Views included in validation scope were incorrectly labeled as TABLE in the report ObjectType column.
Fix: Moved _catalog_object_type_label and _table_kind_map to BaseValidator for shared use. Added cached _table_kind_map and _obj_type helper to DataValidator. Replaced all hardcoded object_type TABLE with kind map lookups that resolve TABLE vs VIEW from catalog metadata. Removed duplicate _table_kind_map from SchemaValidator (now inherited).
MigrationContext: DB2 SYSIBM.SYSTABLES TYPE column: T=TABLE V=VIEW. Azure sys.objects type column: U=TABLE V=VIEW. _catalog_object_type_label normalizes both to full words. The kind map is cached per (schema side) to avoid repeated catalog queries.
AdditionalInfo: Affected ~30 hardcoded occurrences across data.py. Schema validators already used kind maps correctly. DataValidator kind map is cached with thread-safe locking for parallel validation phases.

RuleName: App-team column type overrides reported as INFO acknowledged
RootCause: Columns intentionally widened on Azure per app-team request (e.g. USER_NAME/UID/USERID/USER_ID -> VARCHAR(150)) surfaced as DATATYPE_NAME_MISMATCH (CHARACTER->varchar not in conversion map) and failed datatype_mapping.
Fix: Added ValidationOptions.column_type_overrides (also DV_COLUMN_TYPE_OVERRIDES env / config file); when the Azure base type matches the override the mismatch emits INFO DATATYPE_OVERRIDE_ACKNOWLEDGED with override note in DetailJson instead of error.
MigrationContext: App team approved widening specific columns to VARCHAR(150) during migration.
AdditionalInfo: Keys accept COLUMN or TABLE.COLUMN (case-insensitive); base-type match ignores length.

RuleName: CDC-generated Azure-only objects reported as INFO out-of-scope (target side)
RootCause: Reload_Log / Tables_config tables and usp_DeleteInsertReload / usp_ProcessAllStagingTables procedures are created on Azure by the CDC process and do not exist in DB2; they showed as PRESENCE_MISSING_IN_SOURCE errors.
Fix: Extended presence out-of-scope allowlist with a side field (source/target/any); target-only loop now emits INFO PRESENCE_OUT_OF_SCOPE with a CDC-process note in error_description and DetailJson.
MigrationContext: CDC replication tooling creates staging/reload helper objects on the Azure target only.
AdditionalInfo: Client confirmed; same Info pattern as R023 (EXPLAIN_GET_MSGS source-side).
